A Basque Catholic priest from Navarre, one of the founders of the Society of Jesus, who spent his last ten years as a missionary in Portuguese Asia. He preached in India, Malacca, the Moluccas and Japan.

Xavier met Ignatius of Loyola as a student in Paris, and in 1534 he was one of the first seven Jesuits to take vows at Montmartre. King John III of Portugal asked for missionaries for his empire, and Xavier reached Goa in 1542. In 1545 he went to Malacca, taken by the Portuguese in 1511, and in 1546 and 1547 he worked in the Moluccas, on Ambon and Ternate, the heart of the spice trade.

In Malacca he met a Japanese man named Anjirō, who led him to Japan in 1549. He died in 1552 on Shangchuan Island, off China, while waiting to slip into the country. His body lies in Goa. He was made a saint in 1622. See also Xavier in Goa, Xavier in Japan and the Portuguese capture of Malacca.
